size.note: Wikipedia gives 16–17 cm and a wingspan of 38–40 cm.

habitat: Forages over open, often semi-arid country, including the Kalahari and Okavango when termites emerge, and also over Kruger. Non-breeding birds roost on the wing.
summary: A medium, entirely blackish-brown swift with a short forked tail and very long swept-back wings. A small white or pale grey chin patch is not visible at a distance. It arrives from the north in October in the northern zones and leaves mainly in February and March. The scream has two pitches; Wikipedia says the higher pitch is the female’s. Some birds may remain in the austral winter, but that is not the main pattern.

similar.note: African Black Swift is very similar. Under good light the black back contrasts with paler secondary feathers, and the flight is steadier, with short glides. The chin patch of both species is hard to see.

sources.title: The Atlas of Southern African Birds, Vol. 1 (European Swift)

head.pattern: A small white or pale grey chin patch is not visible from a distance.

viewNotes.note: Blackish brown from below. The pale chin is not visible at a distance.
Blackish brown above, with long swept-back wings and a short fork.
Crescent-shaped wings and a short forked tail. No white rump.

Swifts cling to a vertical surface. They do not settle on the ground, and a normal perched view is not described. The pale chin would be the front mark at a nest, which these birds do not use in southern Africa.
Non-breeding birds roost on the wing, so a perched side view is not the usual Kruger view.

calls.description: Wikipedia says the scream has two pitches and that the higher pitch is the female’s, so the lower pitch is the male’s. The only grade A cut labelled male is a pair inspecting a nest hole, so it was not used.
The higher of the two scream pitches. The catalogue cut is labelled as an adult female calling from the nest. Grade B, Russia, the breeding range.

A loud two-pitch scream, often from a screaming party. This grade A cut is from Sweden, the breeding range, and the filename uses the Swedish name tornseglare. No playable South African call was in the catalogue. It is not labelled by sex.

research.note: Status is a Palearctic migrant. SABAP1 gives arrival in October in the northern zones and departure mainly in February and March, so those months are listed. A few may stay in winter. Newman has no species page for this swift. Chick down and a Kruger recording were not found. The grade A call is from Sweden. The female call is grade B from Russia. The only grade A cut labelled male is a pair at a nest hole, so the male slot is still empty.
